answer: To secure an AI agent economy against Sybil attacks, networks can implement a verifiable computational proof-of-work anchored by a trusted randomness beacon. Just as a single river feeds an inlet with a quantifiable volume of water, an agent must continuously expend costly, non-outsourceable compute to validate its identity. The economic cost to an attacker scales linearly with the number of generated fake nodes, making mass identity fabrication fiscally prohibitive.
